headline: Acting is structured pretending—exploring what it's like to be someone else
universal_truth: Imagining other perspectives builds understanding; empathy can be practiced
fun_facts: Children naturally role-play from around age 2—'pretend play' develops social and cognitive skills
Professional actors report that inhabiting characters changes their own personalities temporarily
Theater emerged in ancient Greece as a religious ritual before becoming entertainment
discussion_questions: What do we learn by pretending to be someone else?
How is acting different from lying?
When do you 'act' in daily life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Children pretend naturally—they become pirates, parents, superheroes. This isn't just play; it's practice for understanding others. Acting formalizes this universal human activity: structured pretending that builds empathy and insight.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Acting is pretending to be someone you're not. That sounds like deception. But actors aren't trying to fool anyone—audiences know it's performance. What's the purpose of this agreed-upon pretending?

options.text: To explore human experience—actors and audiences safely experience emotions and situations outside their own lives
options.response: Yes. Theater is a laboratory for emotion. We can experience tragedy without tragedy, understand villains without villainy. Safe exploration of human possibility.

options.text: Entertainment and escapism—temporary relief from real life
options.response: Entertainment is part of it, but theater's deeper purpose is understanding human experience...

q1.title: Empathy Training
q1.script: Actors must understand characters unlike themselves—their motivations, fears, logic. This requires deep empathy. Studies show acting training increases ability to read emotions and take others' perspectives. Pretending builds understanding.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Empathy Training"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Safe Danger
q2.script: Theater lets audiences feel extreme emotions safely—grief, terror, rage—without real consequences. Aristotle called this 'catharsis': the purging of emotions through art. We experience intensity without damage.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Daily Performance
q3.script: We all act daily. 'Professional you' at work, 'relaxed you' with friends, 'patient you' with family. These aren't fake—they're selections from who you are. Social life requires choosing which self to present.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Imagining other perspectives builds understanding. Acting teaches that empathy can be practiced—we can deliberately explore what it's like to be someone else, and return changed.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 158. Tomorrow, we'll discover words that sound like music—poetry. Until then, notice when you 'perform' different versions of yourself.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Perspective Practice - Be Someone Else
growTrack.activity: Choose someone you struggle to understand. Spend five minutes imagining you are them—their history, their concerns, their logic. Don't judge; just inhabit. What do you understand that you didn't before? Empathy can be practiced.
